paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about. God's people had eyes and ears and a front-row seat to His goodness, and they still never feared Him. The LORD set the sand as a boundary the sea cannot cross, and even the roaring waves obey it (Jeremiah 5:22). But He says of His people, "these people have stubborn and rebellious hearts" (Jeremiah 5:23).

And look at what it cost them. They never said in their hearts, "Let us fear the LORD our God, who gives the rains" (Jeremiah 5:24). The LORD says their own sins have deprived them of His bounty (Jeremiah 5:25). A heart that forgets who gives the gifts ends up grabbing for them, and the passage shows wicked men getting rich on deceit while the fatherless and the needy get ignored (Jeremiah 5:27-28).

So what's the big idea? Fearing the LORD means taking Him seriously, trembling before the One who holds the sea in its place, and letting that shape how we treat people who have nothing (Jeremiah 5:22, 28). The LORD says the prophets prophesy falsely, the priests rule by their own authority, and His people love it so (Jeremiah 5:31). I don't think the question at the end is only for them, baker: "what will you do in the end?" (Jeremiah 5:31)
